If someone asks you this week how you really are, at the gate after church or over suya in the evening, tell them. And if a friend needs a loving word of correction, give it gently. Hope can hold the truth.

line.b: It can also hold an honest answer.

after: Joy and honesty can live in the same friendship.
The God of hope fills people who are still believing, not yet seeing.
days.prayer: God of hope, fill me with joy and peace as I believe, even with my questions. Give me friends who will tell me the truth, and make me that kind of friend. Let your hope rise in me like a shoot from the root of Jesse. In Jesus' name, Amen.
days.question: Who in your life has earned the right to give you an honest answer, and do you let them?

days.title: Joy When the Cost Is Real

body.p: Paul writes this list in pairs. As unknown, and yet well known. as dying, and, behold, we live. Each pair has a hard half and a surprising half, and he does not choose between them.
The middle one is the heart of it. As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing. Not sorrowful first and rejoicing later. Both at the same time, every day, in the same body.

Paul is not exaggerating the cost. He had been beaten, shipwrecked, slandered. The sorrow is not a pose. But neither is the joy. He holds the two together like a man carrying a heavy bag in one hand and a lamp in the other.

And then his voice changes. O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged. After all that suffering, his heart has not shrunk. It has grown. Cost can make people bitter, or it can make them wide.

If following Christ is costing you something real, a friendship, a promotion, a quiet life, say both halves honestly tonight. I am sorrowful. I am also rejoicing. Then open your heart to someone instead of closing it.

line.a: Paul did not choose between sorrow and joy.
line.b: He carried both on the same day.

after: Real cost and real joy can share one day.
Let hardship make your heart wider, not smaller.
days.prayer: Lord, following you has cost me, and I will not pretend it has not. Let me be sorrowful yet always rejoicing. Keep my heart from shrinking under the weight. Enlarge it instead, so that I stay open to the people you have given me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
days.question: Is the cost you are carrying making your heart smaller or larger?

days.title: Joy For the Long Road

body.p: Verse twenty one closes a long list of the works of the flesh, and one of the last words is revellings. Wild parties. The world's version of joy, loud and quick and gone by morning.

Then Paul turns. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace. Joy is the second thing he names, and it is called fruit. Fruit is not produced at a party. It grows slowly, on a branch that stays connected through rain and drought.

The word fruit is also singular. Not fruits. Joy does not come on its own, separated from patience and gentleness. It ripens alongside longsuffering, which is the old word for staying power over a long time.

That is why this is a joy for the long road. Revelry burns hot for a night. Fruit takes seasons. You may not notice it growing at all, until one day you realise you answered with peace where you used to explode.

If this December you are tempted to measure your faith by how excited you feel, look instead for slow fruit. On your commute, ask the Spirit for one more season of growth. against such there is no law, and there is no hurry either.

after: Joy grows on the same branch as patience.
Slow growth is still growth.
days.prayer: Holy Spirit, I want joy that lasts, not a feeling that fades by morning. Grow your fruit in me slowly and deeply, love, joy, peace and longsuffering together. Give me patience with the pace of my own growth, and keep me connected through every season. In Jesus' name, Amen.
days.question: Where have you seen slow fruit growing in you this year?

days.title: Joy At the End of the Day

body.p: Just before this passage, Paul names two women in the church at Philippi who were not getting along, Euodias and Syntyche. Then he asks a trusted friend to help those women which laboured with me in the gospel. They had worked side by side with him. Now they were stuck.

And right after that awkward request comes the most famous line in the letter. Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice. The joy is not written to a calm church. It is written to a church with a quarrel in it.
Paul repeats himself. Again I say. Perhaps he expected them to read it once and think, not today, not with all this going on. So he says it twice.

Then: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. Moderation means gentleness, a willingness not to insist. And the reason is simple. The Lord is near. The quarrel is not the last word.

At the end of today, before you sleep, think of the person you clashed with. Do not replay the argument. Rejoice in the Lord, once and then again, and ask for gentleness for tomorrow. He is at hand, even in a dark bedroom.

line.a: The church had a quarrel in it.

after: Joy can be commanded in a room that is not yet at peace.
The Lord is at hand, so the argument is not the final word.
days.prayer: Lord, at the end of this day I am still unsettled by a conflict. Help me rejoice in you, and then rejoice again. Make my gentleness known, even to the person I clashed with, and let me sleep knowing you are near. In Jesus' name, Amen.
days.question: Who do you need to be gentle with tomorrow?

days.title: Joy For What Comes Next

body.p: Peter had seen Jesus. He had eaten with him, argued with him, denied him and been restored by him on a beach. And he writes to people who never had any of that. Whom having not seen, ye love.
There is no envy in it. Peter sounds almost amazed. These believers, scattered across Asia Minor, have never met Jesus face to face, and still they rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory.

Unspeakable means joy too big for words. It does not come from sight, and it does not wait for the trial to be over. Verse seven calls the trial much more precious than of gold that perisheth, tested by fire and waiting for the appearing of Jesus Christ.
That is where the year ends. Christmas has just celebrated his first coming. Faith now leans toward the second, and the joy belongs to the waiting, not only to the arriving.

Tonight the year turns. Whatever it held, sit for a moment by the window or on the steps outside. You have not seen him. You love him anyway. Carry that into January, and let the next year be lived toward his appearing.

line.b: They loved him unseen, and so can we.

after: Joy unspeakable belongs to people who are still waiting.
Walk into the new year toward his appearing.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, I have not seen you, but I love you. As this year ends, thank you for every way you have kept me through its trials. Let my faith come out of the fire like gold, and fill me with joy as I wait for your appearing in the year ahead. In Jesus' name, Amen.
days.question: As this year ends, what has your unseen love for Jesus carried you through?
